### List

```go
func (s *DockerService) List(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	params DockerListParams,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerEntry]], error)
```

List the containers of the host.

Reads each container through gohai's docker collector, which runs docker ps and
docker inspect. state limits the list to the running or the stopped ones. A host
whose docker does not answer reports skipped. The environment of a container
shows only the names of its variables: osapi never reads their values.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/docker`, and needs the permission
`docker:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A host with a container, `go run docker.go list`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.List(ctx, target, client.DockerListParams{})
```

Only the stopped ones, `go run docker.go list-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.List(ctx, target, client.DockerListParams{State: types.ContainerState("stopped")})
```

### Create

```go
func (s *DockerService) Create(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input DockerCreateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerResult]], error)
```

Create a container.

Runs docker create, which pulls the image when the host does not have it. The
environment goes on docker's standard input, not in its arguments, which each
user of the host can read. auto_start starts the container once it is made. A
container of the name that the host has already is not made again, and reports
changed: false.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/docker`, and needs the permission
`docker:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Create a container, `go run docker.go create`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Create(ctx, target, client.DockerCreateInput{
	Command: []string{"sleep", "300"},
	Image:   "alpine:3.20",
	Name:    "osapitest",
})
```

### Get

```go
func (s *DockerService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerEntry]], error)
```

Get one container.

Reads one container by its name, its ID or the start of its ID. A container that
the host does not have is not found.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/docker/{name}`, and needs the permission
`docker:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A container, `go run docker.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Get(ctx, target, "osapitest")
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *DockerService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerResult]], error)
```

Remove a container.

Runs docker rm -f, which also removes a container that runs: a delete leaves no
container of the name. A container that the host does not have reports changed:
false.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/docker/{name}`, and needs the permission
`docker:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove a container, `go run docker.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Delete(ctx, target, "osapitest")
```

### Exec

```go
func (s *DockerService) Exec(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input DockerExecInput,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerExecResult]], error)
```

Run a command in a container.

Runs docker exec, and answers what the command wrote to standard output and to
standard error, and its exit code. A command that exits with a code other than 0
is an answer, not a failure. It changes what the command changes, which osapi
cannot tell, so it reports changed: true. Its permission is docker:exec, which
only the admin role gets, apart from the docker:execute of start and stop. An
agent with agent.command.enabled false refuses it, as it refuses a command.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/docker/{name}/exec`, and needs the
permission `docker:exec`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Run a command, `go run docker.go exec`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Exec(ctx, target, client.DockerExecInput{
	Command: []string{"echo", "hello"},
	Name:    "osapitest",
})
```

### Start

```go
func (s *DockerService) Start(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerResult]], error)
```

Start a container.

Runs docker start. A container that runs already reports changed: false, and one
that the host does not have is not found.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/docker/{name}/start`, and needs the
permission `docker:execute`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Start a container, `go run docker.go start`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Start(ctx, target, "osapitest")
```

### Stop

```go
func (s *DockerService) Stop(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input DockerStopInput,
) (*Response[Collection[DockerResult]], error)
```

Stop a container.

Runs docker stop, which waits timeout seconds before docker kills the container,
or docker's default of 10 when it is 0. A container that does not run reports
changed: false.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/docker/{name}/stop`, and needs the
permission `docker:execute`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Stop a container, `go run docker.go stop`:

```go
resp, err := c.Docker.Stop(ctx, target, client.DockerStopInput{
	Name:    "osapitest",
	Timeout: 1,
})
```
